downstream_reviews.affected_use: F1 says every standard smooth algebraic chart becomes a holomorphic chart; proof uses compact oriented manifolds, open inclusions and continuous holomorphic modification maps.
snippets: [F1] Analytification and orientation ([[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). A smooth projective complex variety of pure dimension $d$ has an analytification that is a compact Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension $d$, a finite discrete set when $d=0$; every standard smooth algebraic chart becomes a holomorphic chart and every morphism of smooth complex varieties induces a holomorphic, hence continuous, map. A complex manifold carries the canonical orientation for which $(v_1,Jv_1,\dots,v_d,Jv_d)$ is positive on a complex basis, and it is boundaryless; an ample class is represented by a positive closed real $(1,1)$-form, so $X$ and $X'$ are compact Kaehler, hence compact oriented boundaryless $2d$-manifolds, and every open subvariety is an oriented complex submanifold. The analytic topology of a complex algebraic variety is the one of the cited definition, and regular maps are continuous for it.

snippets: [F7] For a smooth closed complex submanifold of projective space, the Fubini–Study form restricts to a positive closed real $(1,1)$-form whose class is the real image of the integral hyperplane class, by the first-Chern comparison ([[lem-first-chern-form-agrees-with-the-topological-line-class]]); for a smooth projective complex variety, the ample class is realized by a positive closed $(1,1)$-form on the compact Kähler analytification ([[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]).

downstream_reviews.affected_use: F1 uses holomorphic coordinates near each SNC point and open complex submanifolds; proof 1.1 applies a local inverse theorem to regular parameters; F3 uses Kähler compact strata.
snippets: [F1] Analytification ([[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]], [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]). $X$ is a compact complex manifold of dimension $d$ with a canonical orientation, $D$ is a reduced divisor with normal crossings, and near every point of $D$ there are holomorphic coordinates $z_1,\dots,z_d$ in which $D$ is $\{z_1\cdots z_s=0\}$ for some $s=s(p)$; each $D^{[a]}$ is a smooth projective complex variety of pure dimension $d-a$ (empty for $a>r$), a morphism of complex varieties induces a holomorphic map, and $U=X\setminus D$ is an open complex submanifold of dimension $d$. Complex-valued smooth forms, the bidegree decomposition, $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ and type are those of [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]], and holomorphic functions on polydiscs are those of [[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]].

[F3] Hodge theory of the compact strata ([[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]], [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]). Let $V$ be a smooth projective complex variety of pure dimension $m$. Then $H^k(V;\mathbb Q)$ carries a functorial rational pure Hodge structure of weight $k$, whose Hodge filtration is the filtration induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration $\Omega^{\ge p}_V$ of the holomorphic de Rham complex; there is a Hodge decomposition $H^k(V;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(V)$ with $H^{p,q}(V)\cong H^q(V,\Omega^p_V)$; the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$; and pullback along a morphism and cup product preserve type. In particular $H^k(V;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$.
downstream_reviews.reason: These are local coordinate assertions, explicitly established after shrinking; compactness, Kähler forms and functoriality remain intact.
